78932.subject: 🐳 DeepSeek's free model beats Claude

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** DeepSeek dropped a model you can download for free that beats Claude Opus 5 on the benchmarks people actually pay for, at a fortieth of the price. Anthropic published eight months of what people were caught doing with Claude, and it's the wildest thing you'll read this week. Amazon is digitally reshaping actors' mouths so dubbing stops looking fake, and a lab in San Francisco pointed a genome model at a tumor and got a vaccine design out the other end.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **DeepSeek:** What did it just make free?

* **Anthropic:** What were people actually building with Claude?

* **Prime Video:** What is it changing about the actors?

* **Cancer:** What did an AI design from one patient's tumor?


----------







----------
## DeepSeek's free model beat Claude Opus 5

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/425779dd-fb9e-4cc7-ace8-6d47dbcd038a/ChatGPT_Image_Sep_11__2026__11_55_51_AM.png?t=1789116983)
Caption: 

DeepSeek [released V4.1 Flash](https://officechai.com/ai/deepseek-v4-1-flash-benchmarks-pricing/), and the weights and the technical report are sitting on Hugging Face for anyone to download.

It has 552 billion parameters but only runs 8 billion of them to read your prompt and 16 billion to write the answer. That's why it's cheap.

* DeepSWE, the software engineering test: 74.2 against Opus 5's 74.0.

* Automation-Bench: 54.8 against Opus 5's 50.3.

* CyberGym, the security one: 88.1 against GPT-5.6 Sol's 84.5.

* Opus 5 still wins where knowledge matters. On HLE it scores 56.3 and Flash gets 36.8.

Opus 5 costs $25 per million output tokens. Flash costs $0.60 off-peak, which is 40 times cheaper for work it does about as well.

DeepSeek is so confident it's retiring its own premium tier. From Sunday every request to V4-Pro gets sent to Flash instead, at Flash prices.

78928.subject: The Agentic Transition Playbook 🧠
78928.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/agentic-transition-playbook

Picture a 50-person R&D organization that came late to AI. Now imagine 2 AI engineers at a competitor, each running a fleet of AI coding agents. On raw throughput, the two can already outpace the fifty. But the math understates their advantage. At two people, there is barely an organization available to slow them down: no management layer or product-manager handoff, no queue of teams waiting on one another. If they also have deep domain expertise and the right architecture underneath them, they are operating in full entrepreneur mode while the 50 stop at every junction. Hence, the Age of the One-Person Company [ https://substack.com/redirect/63a1065b-b229-45db-8693-9f3351959468?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ].
That scenario comes from “The Agentic Awakening,” Liran Eshel and Adam Fisher’s 2026 study for Bessemer Venture Partners of more than twenty engineering organizations. For anyone starting a company, it is the most important passage in the study. Because the asymmetry that has always favored startups, speed over mass, just widened by an order of magnitude. An incumbent still treats its codebase as a moat. To two engineers with AI agents, it’s just an excellent spec. They can rebuild an equivalent product from it, then outbuild the company that wrote it.
It’s worth noting that the same study also contains a warning. Companies that made their engineers 10x faster still could not push organization-level output past roughly 50%. More importantly, the output concentrates brutally: the top 1% of engineers ship 46x the median’s AI-written code. And the product you are building is itself becoming the legacy, because a general-purpose agent with a single domain skill (running, i.e., on Fable 5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/14e99895-e1a2-492c-a5ea-297e92c2b913?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] or Astra [ https://substack.com/redirect/bf4aac10-d561-4b8b-a60a-34462b5065b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]) can now do what an entire specialized SaaS used to do.
The agentic transition is therefore the shift from AI that assists an engineer inside an editor to fleets of autonomous AI agents that write, test, and ship code while humans decide what to build and verify what comes back. For a founder, it completely changes what a company is: how it is built, how it is staffed, how it is shaped, what it sells, and how it is priced. The window opened in the fourth quarter of 2025, when Claude Code 2.0 & Opus 4.5 made coding agents reliable enough to delegate to. 10 months later, the public market has repriced software as a category, and the foundation labs have moved into the application layer. Salesforce is now even spending close to $300 million on Anthropic tokens this year while totally freezing engineering hires.
